faqs.q: Do I need planning permission for a home charge point?
faqs.a: Almost never for a standard domestic installation. We'll flag it if your property is an exception, such as a listed building.

faqs.q: How long does installation take?
faqs.a: Most home installs are done within half a day, depending on cable run length and whether any consumer unit work is needed.

faqs.q: What if my consumer unit can't handle a charger?
faqs.a: We check this during the free survey. If an upgrade is needed, we'll quote for it alongside the charger install.

faqs.q: Are smart chargers a legal requirement?
faqs.a: Yes — since 2022, new home and workplace chargers in Great Britain must have smart charging capability by law. All our installs meet this.

faqs.q: Can you install chargers for businesses and fleets?
faqs.a: Yes, including multi-charger workplace setups with load balancing so you're not paying to upgrade your whole supply unnecessarily.

benefit: Charge Your EV at Home, Safely & Fast

deepDive.heading: What Actually Happens During an EV Charger Install
paragraphs: It starts with the free survey, not the fitting — we check your incoming supply, existing consumer unit, and the cable route between the board and where the charger's going, because that's what decides the real cost and timeline, not the charger itself.

On install day, we run the cable, mount the unit, and connect it into your consumer unit — upgrading the board first if the survey flagged it as necessary. Every charger is then load-tested, commissioned, and certified before we hand it over.

Since 2022, every new home and workplace charger in Great Britain is legally required to have smart charging capability, meaning it can be scheduled and monitored remotely — that's standard on everything we fit, not an optional extra.

concerns.q: Will my existing electrics actually cope with a charger?
concerns.a: That's exactly what the free survey is for — we check your supply and consumer unit before quoting, so there are no surprises once work starts.

concerns.q: How long will the power be off for?
concerns.a: Usually a short isolation while we connect into the consumer unit, not an all-day outage — we'll tell you the expected window before we start.

concerns.q: How long does the whole job take?
concerns.a: Most home installs are done within half a day, start to finish.

faqs.q: How long does a full rewire take?
faqs.a: A typical two or three-bedroom tenement flat takes around a week. We'll give you an exact timeline once we've surveyed the property.

faqs.q: Do I need to move out during a rewire?
faqs.a: Not always for a partial rewire, but for a full rewire it's usually easier to have the property empty. We'll talk through the options for your specific job.

faqs.q: Will you make good after chasing walls?
faqs.a: We fill and make good all channels we cut. If you need a full plaster skim afterwards, we can recommend a plasterer we work with regularly.

faqs.q: Can a business rewire be done without closing?
faqs.a: Often yes, by phasing the work area by area or working out of hours — we'll scope this properly at quote stage.

faqs.q: Is the work certified?
faqs.a: Yes, every rewire is tested to BS7671 and certified on completion.

benefit: Safe, Modern Wiring You Can Trust

deepDive.heading: What Does a Full Rewire Actually Involve?
paragraphs: A rewire happens in two stages: first fix, where we run new cabling through walls, floors, and ceilings to every socket, switch, and light position; and second fix, where we connect and terminate everything — sockets, switches, the consumer unit — once walls are closed up again. Between the two, everything is tested to BS7671 before we sign it off.

Glasgow's tenement and period flats bring their own quirks that a generic rewire quote won't account for — lath-and-plaster walls behave differently to modern stud walls when it comes to chasing cable routes, and shared stairwells or factor-managed common areas sometimes need a quick word with the factor before we touch anything communal. We've worked enough of these properties across the city to know which questions to ask before we start, not halfway through.

concerns.q: Do I need a full rewire, or would a partial one do?
concerns.a: It depends on the property — sometimes a targeted partial rewire of the affected circuits is genuinely enough. We'll tell you honestly which one your property needs after a proper look, not just upsell the bigger job.

concerns.q: Is my current wiring actually safe to keep using?
concerns.a: That's what an EICR is for — if you're not sure, we'd rather test it properly than guess. It tells you exactly what's safe, what's borderline, and what needs attention now.

concerns.q: Will the power be off during the work?
concerns.a: Yes, while we connect the new wiring in — we agree the timing with you in advance and keep it to the minimum needed.

concerns.q: How long will it actually take?
concerns.a: A typical two or three-bedroom flat takes around a week. Larger or occupied properties take longer, which we'll scope honestly at survey stage.

commonProblems: Old or outdated wiring that's never been upgraded

faqs.q: How often does a rented property need an EICR in Scotland?
faqs.a: At least every 5 years, or at change of tenancy if the previous report is due to expire — it's a legal requirement under the Repairing Standard.

faqs.q: How long does testing take?
faqs.a: A typical flat or house takes 2–4 hours on site. Larger commercial properties take longer, which we'll scope in advance.

faqs.q: What happens if the property fails?
faqs.a: We list every issue found, rated by severity, and can quote for the remedial work on the spot so you're not left chasing a second contractor.

faqs.q: Do I get the certificate the same day?
faqs.a: You'll get a verbal summary on site, with the full written EICR following shortly after.

faqs.q: Is an EICR a legal requirement for landlords?
faqs.a: Yes, under the Scottish Repairing Standard, private landlords must hold a satisfactory EICR.

deepDive.heading: What We Actually Test During an EICR
paragraphs: An EICR isn't a quick visual once-over — it's a full inspection combining a visual check of accessible wiring and fittings with 'dead testing' (checked with the power off, covering continuity, insulation resistance, and earthing) and 'live testing' (checked with the power on, covering RCD trip times and polarity).

Every issue we find gets a code, not just a pass/fail: C1 means danger present, needing action immediately; C2 means potentially dangerous, needing to be addressed urgently; C3 is an improvement recommended but not a compliance failure; and FI means further investigation is needed. We explain what each one actually means for your property in plain English on the day, not just in a report you get later.

concerns.q: Is my current installation actually safe to keep using?
concerns.a: That's precisely what the test tells you — a clear pass, or a specific list of what needs attention, rated by how urgent it is. No guessing.

concerns.q: How long will the test take?
concerns.a: A typical flat or house takes 2–4 hours on site. Larger commercial properties take longer, which we'll scope in advance.

concerns.q: What if it doesn't pass?
concerns.a: We list every issue found, rated by severity, and can quote for the remedial work on the spot — you're not left chasing a second contractor to fix what we found.

commonProblems: Out of date or missing electrical certificates
No record of when the property was last tested

Your board has no RCD (residual current device) protection

faqs.q: How long does an upgrade take?
faqs.a: Most homes are done in half a day to a full day, depending on how many circuits need re-terminating.

faqs.q: Will the power be off during the work?
faqs.a: Yes, temporarily — we'll agree a time that works for you and keep the power-down window as short as possible.

faqs.q: Do I need a new consumer unit if mine fails an EICR?
faqs.a: If the EICR marks it as a serious risk (C1/C2), yes — we can quote for the upgrade at the same visit.

faqs.q: What size consumer unit do I need?
faqs.a: It depends on your existing circuits and any future additions like an EV charger — we work this out during the free survey.

faqs.q: Is the upgrade certified?
faqs.a: Yes, every consumer unit upgrade is tested and certified on completion.

benefit: A Safer Fuse Board, Sorted Same Day

deepDive.heading: RCDs, RCBOs, and Why Your Board Actually Matters
paragraphs: An old rewireable fuse box protects your wiring from overheating — that's it. It does nothing to protect a person from electric shock, because it has no RCD (residual current device) protection, which is why boards like these are one of the most common issues we flag on an EICR.

A modern consumer unit fits RCDs or RCBOs (a combined breaker and RCD per circuit) as standard, which cut the power in milliseconds if they detect current leaking somewhere it shouldn't — like through a person. We size and split circuits properly across the board so one nuisance trip doesn't take out your whole house, which is the other common complaint we hear about old or badly-specified boards.

concerns.q: Do I need a whole new board, or can mine be repaired?
concerns.a: If it's an old rewireable fuse box with no RCD protection, repairing it isn't really an option — it needs replacing to meet current safety standards. If it's a modern board with one faulty part, sometimes a repair genuinely is enough, and we'll tell you honestly which applies.

concerns.q: Is my current board safe to keep using in the meantime?
concerns.a: We'll tell you straight during the survey — if it's a serious risk we won't let you sit on it, but plenty of ageing boards are fine to use short-term while you plan the upgrade.

concerns.q: Will the power be off during the work?
concerns.a: Yes, temporarily — we agree a time that works for you and keep the power-down window as short as possible.

concerns.q: How long does it actually take?
concerns.a: Most homes are done in half a day to a full day, depending on how many circuits need re-terminating.

commonProblems: Lights tripping when other appliances switch on
Power outages traced back to an old or overloaded board

deepDive.heading: First Fix vs Second Fix, Explained
paragraphs: If you've not been through a build before, 'first fix' and 'second fix' get thrown around a lot without much explanation. First fix happens once the structure's up but before walls are closed — we run all the cabling to every socket, switch, and light position, coordinated with the builder so nothing gets boarded over before it's in place.

Second fix comes after plastering and decoration — we come back to actually terminate everything: fitting sockets, switches, light fittings, and connecting into the consumer unit. Getting the timing of both right with your builder is what keeps an extension on schedule, which is why we'd rather be brought in at the planning stage than after first fix should have already happened.

concerns.q: Will the power need to be isolated while you work?
concerns.a: Only for the specific circuits we're connecting into, and usually briefly — the rest of your home stays powered as normal.

concerns.q: How long does first fix take?

deepDive.heading: Planning Your Kitchen's Electrics Before the Units Go In
paragraphs: Kitchens carry more electrical load than any other room in the house, so getting the plan right before first fix matters more here than almost anywhere else. Ovens, hobs, and induction hobs in particular need their own dedicated circuit sized to that specific appliance — not shared with your general sockets — which is something we agree with you and your kitchen fitter before any cabinets go in.

Socket and lighting positions need to be locked in at first fix too, ideally before the units are ordered, since moving a socket after the cabinets are fitted means undoing tiling and worktops. Under-cabinet and feature lighting is easiest to wire in cleanly at this stage as well, so there's no visible cabling once everything's installed.

concerns.q: Do I need a full re-wire of the kitchen, or just new circuits for the appliances?
concerns.a: Usually just dedicated circuits for the new appliances and any layout changes — a full kitchen rewire is only needed if the existing wiring itself is old or undersized. We'll tell you honestly which applies once we've seen it.

concerns.q: How long will it take?

intro: Portable Appliance Testing keeps staff, tenants, and customers safe from faulty electrical equipment, and gives you the paperwork insurers and letting agents ask for. We test everything from office kit to kitchen appliances on a schedule that suits your business, not ours.

faqs.q: Is PAT testing a legal requirement?
faqs.a: There's no single law naming PAT testing directly, but the Electricity at Work Regulations 1989 require equipment to be maintained safely — PAT testing is the standard, recognised way to demonstrate that. Many insurers and letting agents treat it as effectively mandatory.

faqs.q: How often does testing need to be done?
faqs.a: It depends on the equipment and environment — office IT equipment needs testing less often than kitchen appliances or tools on a building site. We'll recommend a schedule for your specific setup.

faqs.q: How long does a PAT test take?
faqs.a: A small office is usually done within a couple of hours. Larger sites or rental portfolios take longer — we'll give you a time estimate once we know roughly how many items are involved.

faqs.q: What happens if something fails?
faqs.a: We label it clearly as failed, explain why, and quote for repair or safe disposal. Everything else in the batch is tested and certified as normal.

faqs.q: Do you test both landlord and business equipment?
faqs.a: Yes — we cover rented residential properties, offices, retail units, and workshops across Glasgow and the surrounding areas.

benefit: Tested, Labelled, and Certified — No Guesswork

deepDive.heading: What Actually Gets Checked During PAT Testing
paragraphs: PAT testing is two steps, not one: a visual inspection of the plug, cable, and casing for obvious damage, followed by an electrical test of earth continuity, insulation resistance, and — where relevant — polarity. Most failures are caught at the visual stage, before the equipment is even plugged into a tester.

Every item gets a pass or fail label with the date, so it's obvious at a glance what's current and what's due. We keep a digital register alongside the physical labels, so if a certificate ever needs to be produced for an insurer, letting agent, or auditor, it's a five-minute job to pull it up rather than a search through a filing cabinet.

concerns.q: Will testing disrupt our working day?
concerns.a: We can test around your hours, including early mornings, evenings, or between tenancies, so equipment isn't out of use when you need it.

concerns.q: Do you provide proof for our insurer?
concerns.a: Yes, every job comes with a certificate and item-by-item register that insurers and letting agents recognise.

faqs.q: Do landlords in Scotland legally need an EICR?
faqs.a: Yes — it's a legal requirement under the Repairing Standard for private landlords in Scotland to have a satisfactory Electrical Installation Condition Report, generally renewed at least every five years.

faqs.q: What happens if my property fails?

deepDive.heading: Staying Compliant Without Chasing Renewal Dates
paragraphs: The five-yearly EICR renewal is the deadline most landlords know about, but the bigger risk is usually smaller and more avoidable: a certificate that quietly lapses because nobody was tracking the date, discovered only when a tenant complains or a letting agent asks for proof. We flag upcoming renewals well ahead of time rather than leaving you to remember.

For landlords with more than one property, the real value is having a single point of contact who knows the portfolio, not a different tradesperson booked fresh for every address. We keep a record of what's been inspected, what's outstanding, and what's coming up, so a renewal is a phone call rather than a scramble.

concerns.q: Will a failed inspection delay my letting?
concerns.a: Only if remedial work is genuinely needed for safety — we'll always tell you plainly what's required and how quickly it can realistically be turned around.

concerns.q: Do you deal directly with letting agents?

name: Smoke & Heat Alarm Installation
shortDesc: Interlinked smoke, heat and CO alarm installation to Scottish tenement and fire safety standards.
intro: Since 2022, every home in Scotland has been required to have interlinked smoke, heat, and carbon monoxide alarms, wherever they're needed. We install and wire systems correctly the first time, whether that's a straightforward retrofit or coordinated as part of a wider rewire.
highlights: Interlinked smoke, heat, and CO alarm systems
Mains-wired and wireless-interlinked options
Sited correctly to current Scottish fire safety standards
Certification confirming the installation meets the standard
whyUs: We know exactly what the Scottish interlinked alarm standard actually requires
Alarms wired in as part of any rewire or consumer unit job at no extra hassle
Wireless-interlink options where full rewiring isn't practical
Clear certification confirming your home meets the standard
signs: You've been told your current alarms aren't interlinked and don't meet the standard
You're selling your home and need compliant alarms for the sale
You're renovating and want alarms wired in properly, not bolted on afterwards
Your smoke alarms are battery-only and over ten years old
You need a carbon monoxide alarm near a boiler, fire, or flue

faqs.q: What does the Scottish interlinked alarm standard actually require?
faqs.a: Broadly: one smoke alarm in the room most used during the day, one in every circulation space like hallways and landings, a heat alarm in the kitchen, and a carbon monoxide alarm anywhere there's a fuel-burning appliance — all interlinked, so if one goes off, they all do.

faqs.q: Do the alarms have to be mains-wired?
faqs.a: Ideally yes, but where rewiring isn't practical, long-life tamper-proof battery alarms that interlink wirelessly are an accepted alternative under the standard.

faqs.q: Is this a legal requirement or just a recommendation?
faqs.a: It's a legal requirement for all homes in Scotland, regardless of tenure — owner-occupied, rented, or social housing.

faqs.q: Can you fit this alongside other electrical work?
faqs.a: Yes, it's often most efficient to have interlinked alarms wired in as part of a rewire or consumer unit upgrade — ask us to include it when you get a quote for other work.

faqs.q: How long does installation take?
faqs.a: A straightforward retrofit in an average home is usually completed within a day.

benefit: Interlinked Alarms, Fitted to the Scottish Standard

deepDive.heading: Getting the Interlinked Alarm Standard Right
paragraphs: The most common mistake we find isn't a missing alarm — it's alarms that exist but aren't actually interlinked, or a heat alarm in the kitchen that's been swapped for a smoke alarm at some point, which isn't compliant. We start every job by checking what's already there against the standard, not assuming a full new system is needed.

Where mains wiring back to the consumer unit is straightforward, that's usually the best long-term option. In tenement flats or properties where chasing cable routes would mean significant disruption, a wireless-interlinked system using long-life alarms meets the same standard with far less work — we'll be upfront about which makes sense for your property before quoting.

concerns.q: Will this involve chasing walls or major disruption?
concerns.a: Only if you specifically want full mains wiring — wireless-interlinked alarms are a genuine, compliant alternative with minimal disruption.

concerns.q: Do I need this if I'm not selling or renting?
concerns.a: Yes, the standard applies to all homes in Scotland regardless of whether you're selling, letting, or simply living in the property.

ctaLabel: Check My Alarms Meet the Standard

name: Electrical Fault Finding & Repairs
shortDesc: Diagnosing and fixing tripping circuits, dead sockets, and intermittent electrical faults.
intro: A tripping circuit or a socket that's gone dead is rarely random — there's a specific cause, and finding it properly the first time saves you paying for the same callout twice. We trace faults systematically rather than guessing, then fix the actual problem.
highlights: Systematic fault diagnosis, not guesswork
Tripping circuits, dead sockets, and intermittent faults
Same electrician from diagnosis through to repair
Clear explanation of what caused it and why
whyUs: We trace faults to their actual cause, not just the nearest symptom
Same-day response available for genuinely urgent faults
Straight answers about whether it's a quick fix or a bigger underlying issue
Every repair tested before we consider the job done
signs: A circuit trips repeatedly, especially at the same time or with the same appliance
A socket or switch has stopped working with no obvious cause
Lights flicker, dim, or buzz intermittently
You can smell burning or see scorch marks near a socket or switch
An appliance trips the whole circuit rather than just its own plug

faqs.q: Why does my circuit keep tripping?
faqs.a: It's usually one of a few things: a faulty appliance, damaged cable, a failing RCD, or a circuit that's simply overloaded. We isolate which one it is systematically rather than replacing parts until it stops.

faqs.q: Is a tripping circuit an emergency?
faqs.a: Not always, but it shouldn't be ignored — repeated tripping is often an early warning sign. If it's happening frequently or you can smell burning, treat it as urgent and get in touch straight away.

faqs.q: How quickly can you get to a fault?
faqs.a: We aim for same-day response on genuine faults. Call rather than email if it's urgent — it's the fastest way to get a time confirmed.

faqs.q: Will you know what's wrong before you arrive?
faqs.a: Sometimes we can narrow it down over the phone, but most faults need an on-site diagnosis to trace properly — we don't guess and hope.

faqs.q: Do you fix the fault on the same visit?
faqs.a: In most cases yes, once it's diagnosed. If parts need ordering or it turns out to be a bigger job, we'll explain that clearly and quote before doing anything further.

benefit: The Actual Cause Found, Not Just the Nearest Symptom

deepDive.heading: How We Actually Trace an Electrical Fault
paragraphs: Fault finding starts with questions, not tools — when it happens, what's plugged in at the time, whether it's one circuit or several. That narrows things down before we even open the consumer unit. From there we isolate circuits one at a time, testing insulation resistance and continuity to find exactly where the fault is, rather than replacing the first suspicious-looking component.

The reason this matters is that a quick fix aimed at the wrong cause just brings the customer back a few weeks later with the same trip. We'd rather spend the extra twenty minutes tracing it properly and fix it once.

concerns.q: What if you can't find the fault straight away?
concerns.a: Intermittent faults can take longer to isolate — we'll be honest if a job needs a second visit rather than pushing through and guessing.

concerns.q: Will I be without power while you work?
concerns.a: Only the affected circuit is usually isolated, not the whole property, and we'll tell you what to expect before starting.

name: Domestic Lighting Installation
shortDesc: Downlights, spotlights, pendants and LED strip lighting for homes across Glasgow.
intro: Good lighting changes how a room actually feels, not just how bright it is. We plan layouts properly before fitting anything — downlights, spotlights, pendants, or LED strip — so the finished result looks intentional, not scattered.
highlights: Downlights, spotlights, and pendant fittings
LED strip lighting for kitchens, stairs, and feature walls
Layouts planned before installation, not fitted ad-hoc
Dimmer and smart lighting control options
whyUs: We plan the layout with you before any cable goes in, not after
Clean finishes with no visible cabling or patched ceilings
Dimmer and smart control wiring done properly, not bodged in
Same-day quotes for straightforward room lighting upgrades
signs: You're replacing a single central pendant with proper downlighting
You want LED strip lighting under units, on stairs, or along a feature wall
Your current lighting leaves obvious dark spots in a room
You're renovating and want lighting planned in from the start
You want dimmer switches or smart control added

faqs.q: How many downlights does a typical room need?
faqs.a: It depends on room size, ceiling height, and what the room's used for — we work this out properly during the quote rather than applying a generic rule of thumb.

faqs.q: Can you add lighting without ripping up the ceiling?
faqs.a: In most cases yes, particularly with suspended or plasterboard ceilings — we'll assess your specific ceiling type and explain the options honestly.

faqs.q: Do you fit smart or app-controlled lighting?
faqs.a: Yes, including smart dimmer switches and app-controlled systems, wired in properly rather than relying on plug-in adapters.

faqs.q: Can you match new lighting to existing circuits?
faqs.a: Yes, though we'll check the existing circuit can safely take the extra load before adding to it, rather than assuming it can.

faqs.q: How long does a typical room take?
faqs.a: A single room is usually a day or less; multi-room lighting projects take longer, and we'll confirm a timeline once we've seen the layout you want.

benefit: Lighting That's Planned, Not Just Fitted

deepDive.heading: Why Lighting Layout Matters More Than the Fittings Themselves
paragraphs: The single biggest difference between lighting that looks professional and lighting that looks patched-in is planning the layout before any cable goes in — working out spacing, beam angles, and where dark spots will actually fall, rather than fitting downlights in a rough grid and hoping.

Circuit capacity matters too, particularly when adding LED strip or multiple new fittings to an existing lighting circuit — we check what a circuit can safely carry before adding to it, rather than discovering a problem after the ceiling's closed back up.

concerns.q: Will you make good after fitting downlights?
concerns.a: Yes, we patch and make good any ceiling work, though a full paint touch-up is down to you or your decorator afterwards.

concerns.q: What if I'm not sure exactly what I want yet?
concerns.a: That's fine — we can talk through options and show examples during the quote visit rather than needing a finished plan upfront.

name: Security Lighting Installation
shortDesc: PIR floodlights and motion-activated security lighting for homes and businesses.
intro: Motion-activated lighting is one of the simplest, most effective deterrents for a property — and one of the most commonly fitted badly, aimed wrong or wired without proper weatherproofing. We install security lighting that actually triggers when and where it should.
highlights: PIR motion-activated floodlights and wall lights
Correctly weatherproofed outdoor wiring
Sensor sensitivity and angle set up on-site, not left default
Domestic and commercial premises covered
whyUs: Sensors positioned and calibrated on-site so they trigger correctly
All outdoor wiring properly weatherproofed, not just outdoor-rated fittings
Domestic driveways through to full commercial perimeter lighting
Straightforward advice on where lighting actually adds security value
signs: You've had break-ins or attempted break-ins nearby
Your driveway, side passage, or back garden is unlit at night
Your current security light triggers constantly or barely at all
You're installing CCTV and want matching motion lighting
A business premises has unlit areas around entrances or car parks

faqs.q: Where should security lighting actually be positioned?
faqs.a: Entry points and approach routes matter more than covering every inch of a garden — we'll walk the property with you and recommend positions based on how someone would actually approach it.

faqs.q: Why does my current sensor light trigger constantly?
faqs.a: Usually poor sensitivity calibration or a sensor picking up passing traffic, trees, or animals — this is adjustable, and we'll set it correctly rather than leaving it on factory default.

faqs.q: Can you wire lighting to a switch as well as a sensor?
faqs.a: Yes, a manual override switch alongside the PIR sensor is a common and sensible setup.

faqs.q: Do you install lighting for commercial premises?
faqs.a: Yes, from single entrance floodlights to full perimeter lighting for commercial and industrial sites.

faqs.q: Is outdoor electrical wiring different from indoor?
faqs.a: Yes — it needs to be properly rated and protected against water ingress, which is a common cause of failed outdoor lighting we're called out to fix.

benefit: Lighting That Actually Triggers When It Should

deepDive.heading: Getting Sensor Positioning and Sensitivity Right
paragraphs: Most complaints we hear about existing security lighting come down to positioning and calibration, not the fitting itself — a sensor aimed too high misses people at ground level, while one aimed at a road or a neighbour's garden triggers constantly on passing traffic that has nothing to do with your property.
We set sensitivity and range during installation based on the actual space, then check it works as intended before we finish the job, rather than leaving factory defaults for you to adjust yourself.

concerns.q: Will the lighting disturb neighbours?
concerns.a: We angle and range sensors to cover your property specifically, which minimises spill onto neighbouring gardens or windows.

concerns.q: Can this be added to an existing outdoor circuit?
concerns.a: Often yes, provided the circuit has capacity — we'll check this as part of the quote.

name: Garden & Outdoor Lighting
shortDesc: Feature, path, and patio lighting design and installation for gardens across Glasgow.
intro: Outdoor lighting is as much about design as wiring — the difference between a garden that looks flat after dark and one that actually gets used in the evening. We plan feature, path, and patio lighting properly, then install it to a genuinely weatherproof standard.
highlights: Path, step, and patio lighting
Feature lighting for trees, planting, and garden structures
Low-voltage and mains-wired options
Weatherproof, IP-rated fittings and cable throughout
whyUs: Lighting planned around how the garden's actually used in the evening
Low-voltage systems available where a full mains circuit isn't needed
Cable runs buried and protected properly, not just laid on the surface
Fittings chosen to suit the garden, not just the cheapest option
signs: You want to actually use your garden or patio in the evenings
Steps or paths are a trip hazard once it's dark
You've got trees, planting, or a feature you'd like lit at night
You're landscaping and want lighting planned in before the hard work goes in
Existing garden lighting has failed or was never wired properly

faqs.q: Does garden lighting need a new circuit?
faqs.a: It depends on scale — a few low-voltage fittings can often run from a transformer off an existing supply, while larger schemes usually justify their own dedicated outdoor circuit.

faqs.q: Is low-voltage lighting as good as mains-wired?
faqs.a: For most garden feature and path lighting, yes — it's safer to install, cheaper to run, and perfectly capable for the brightness most gardens need.

faqs.q: How deep does outdoor cable need to be buried?
faqs.a: It depends on the cable type and voltage, but it always needs proper mechanical protection, not just laid under turf — we'll do this correctly and can show you where cable runs are for future reference.

faqs.q: Can lighting be added before or after landscaping?
faqs.a: Before is easier and cheaper if you know roughly what you want — cable can go in during groundworks rather than being dug in afterwards.

faqs.q: Do you offer timers or smart controls for garden lighting?
faqs.a: Yes, timers, photocell sensors, and app-controlled options are all available depending on how hands-off you want it to be.

benefit: A Garden That Actually Gets Used After Dark

deepDive.heading: Planning Garden Lighting Before the Cable Goes In
paragraphs: The gardens that end up looking good at night are almost always the ones where lighting was planned before any cable was buried — deciding what to highlight, what to leave dark, and where people will actually walk, rather than adding fittings piecemeal after the landscaping's finished.

Low-voltage systems cover most of what a typical garden needs — path lighting, uplighters for trees or planting, and step lighting — run safely off a transformer without needing a full new mains circuit. Larger schemes, especially those combined with power for a garden room or hot tub, usually justify a dedicated outdoor circuit instead, and we'll advise honestly on which your garden actually needs.

concerns.q: Will digging in cable disturb my existing landscaping?
concerns.a: We plan cable routes to minimise disruption, and where possible we coordinate with any landscaping work already planned so it's done once, not twice.

concerns.q: Is outdoor lighting expensive to run?
concerns.a: Low-voltage LED garden lighting costs very little to run — the bigger cost is usually the initial design and installation, not the electricity.

name: New Socket & Switch Installations
shortDesc: Additional sockets, switches, and USB points fitted cleanly to existing circuits.
intro: Not enough sockets in a room is one of the most common — and most fixable — problems in older homes. We add sockets, switches, and USB points where you actually need them, checked against your existing circuit capacity so nothing gets overloaded.
highlights: New sockets, switches, and USB charging points
Circuit capacity checked before adding any new point
Clean chasing and finishing, not surface-mounted trunking
Relocations for sockets in awkward or outdated positions
whyUs: We check what a circuit can actually take before adding to it
Chased-in cabling as standard, not surface trunking unless you prefer it
Awkwardly placed sockets relocated properly, not just extended with cable
Small jobs given the same attention as larger ones
signs: You're relying on extension leads or adapters because there aren't enough sockets
A room has sockets in the wrong place for how furniture's actually arranged
You want USB charging points added without an adapter
A switch is awkwardly positioned or you want two-way switching added
You're setting up a home office and need sockets in a specific layout

faqs.q: Can any circuit take an extra socket?
faqs.a: Usually yes for one or two additional points, but we check the circuit's existing load first — this is a two-minute check that avoids overloading it.

faqs.q: Will you need to chase into the wall?
faqs.a: For a clean finish, yes in most cases — we chase cable in and make good afterwards rather than leaving surface-mounted trunking, unless you specifically prefer that option.

faqs.q: Can you add USB sockets without changing the whole socket?
faqs.a: Yes, combined socket-and-USB faceplates are a straightforward swap in most cases.

faqs.q: How long does adding one or two sockets take?
faqs.a: Usually a few hours including making good, depending on the cable route needed.

faqs.q: Can you move a socket rather than add a new one?
faqs.a: Yes — if a socket's badly positioned, relocating it properly is often better than extending cable to a new point nearby.

benefit: Sockets Where You Actually Need Them

deepDive.heading: Why We Check Circuit Load Before Adding a Socket
paragraphs: Adding a socket looks simple from the outside, but the question that actually matters is what's already running on that circuit — a ring main with several heavy appliances already on it behaves differently to a lightly loaded circuit in a spare room. We check this before quoting, not after fitting.

Where a socket's badly positioned rather than simply missing, the better fix is usually relocating it properly — running fresh cable to the right spot and capping off the old point — rather than extending cable across a wall to reach a new position, which tends to look and perform worse long term.

concerns.q: Will you leave visible cable on the wall?
concerns.a: Not unless you specifically ask for surface trunking — our default is to chase cable in and make good.

concerns.q: Is this classed as notifiable work?
concerns.a: Adding sockets to an existing circuit generally isn't notifiable in the way a new circuit or consumer unit change is, but we'll confirm this for your specific job.

name: Electric Heating & Thermostats
shortDesc: Electric radiators, panel heaters, and smart thermostat installation for homes without gas.
intro: For properties without mains gas — flats, garden rooms, outbuildings, and off-grid homes — electric heating done properly is efficient, controllable, and a lot better than a plug-in heater on an extension lead. We install and wire heating on its own dedicated, correctly sized circuit.
highlights: Electric radiators and panel heaters on dedicated circuits
Smart thermostats, including Hive and similar systems
Correctly sized circuits, not plug-in heaters on shared sockets
Garden room, outbuilding, and off-grid heating
whyUs: Every heater sized to a properly calculated circuit, not guessed
Smart thermostat setup and app configuration included
Experience wiring heating into garden rooms and outbuildings
Straight advice on running costs, not just the install
signs: You're relying on plug-in heaters because a room has no fixed heating
You're heating a garden room, home office, or outbuilding
Your property has no mains gas connection
You want a smart thermostat like Hive fitted and set up properly
Old storage heaters need replacing with something more controllable

faqs.q: Is electric heating expensive to run compared to gas?
faqs.a: Per unit of energy it's generally more expensive than gas, but for smaller spaces, garden rooms, or properties without a gas connection, a properly sized and controlled system can still be the most practical option.

faqs.q: Do panel heaters need their own circuit?
faqs.a: For anything beyond a single small heater, yes — running heating from a general socket circuit risks overloading it, which is why we size a dedicated circuit to the heater's actual demand.

faqs.q: Can you fit and set up a Hive thermostat?
faqs.a: Yes, including the electrical wiring and the app configuration, so it's genuinely ready to use when we leave, not just physically installed.

faqs.q: Can you wire heating into a garden room or outbuilding?
faqs.a: Yes, this is a common job for us — including running the supply out from the main property if that's needed.

faqs.q: How do I know what size heater a room needs?
faqs.a: It depends on room size, insulation, and how it's used — we'll size this properly during the quote rather than fitting whatever's convenient.

benefit: Heating Sized and Wired Properly, Not Bolted On

deepDive.heading: Sizing Electric Heating to the Room, Not the Nearest Heater
paragraphs: The most common issue we find with electric heating isn't the heater itself — it's an undersized circuit trying to run it, often because it was plugged into a general socket circuit rather than given a dedicated supply. We calculate the actual load a room's heating will draw before deciding on cable size and circuit protection.

Garden rooms and outbuildings need particular thought, since the supply often has to run some distance from the main property, buried or ducted correctly along the way. Getting the cable sizing and protection right at that stage avoids voltage drop and nuisance tripping once the heating's actually in use.

concerns.q: Will this need a new circuit from the consumer unit?
concerns.a: In most cases yes, sized specifically to the heating load — we'll confirm this and any consumer unit capacity implications during the quote.

concerns.q: Can you replace old storage heaters?
concerns.a: Yes, including removing the old units and wiring in modern, more controllable panel heaters or radiators in their place.

shortDesc: Structured data cabling for home offices, and commercial network installations.
intro: Wi-Fi doesn't always cut it for a proper home office or a busy commercial space. We install structured data cabling — properly routed, terminated, and tested — so your network is reliable, not held together by extenders and hope.
highlights: Structured Cat6 data cabling for home and office
Network points terminated and tested, not just run
Home office and commercial installations
Coordinated with electrical first-fix on new builds and renovations
whyUs: Every cable run tested and certified, not just pushed through a wall
Data points positioned properly for how the space is actually used
Coordinated with electrical work so it's planned in, not an afterthought
Commercial network installs scheduled around your operating hours
signs: Wi-Fi doesn't reach reliably to a home office or specific room
You're setting up a business and need a structured network from scratch
You're renovating and want data points wired in properly, not added later
Current cabling is a mix of extenders and visible trailing cable
You need multiple reliable network points for work-from-home setups

faqs.q: Is wired data cabling better than Wi-Fi?
faqs.a: For anything needing consistent speed and reliability — video calls, larger file transfers, business network traffic — yes, a wired point is more dependable than relying on Wi-Fi signal strength alone.

faqs.q: What cable standard do you install?
faqs.a: Cat6 as standard, which comfortably covers current and near-future network speeds for home and most commercial use.

faqs.q: Can this be added to an existing home without major disruption?
faqs.a: In most cases yes, particularly where there's loft or underfloor access to route cable through — we'll assess your specific property and explain the realistic options.

faqs.q: Do you test the cabling once it's installed?
faqs.a: Yes, every point is tested for continuity and performance before we consider the job finished, not just visually checked.

faqs.q: Can you coordinate this with other electrical work?
faqs.a: Yes, it's often most efficient to plan data cabling alongside a rewire, extension, or office fit-out, so runs go in at the same time as electrical first-fix.

benefit: A Network You Can Actually Rely On

deepDive.heading: Why Wired Points Still Matter in a Wi-Fi Home or Office
paragraphs: Wi-Fi has got better, but it still degrades with distance, walls, and interference in a way a wired point simply doesn't. For a home office, a business relying on point-of-sale systems, or anywhere multiple people are on video calls at once, a couple of properly installed data points solve problems that a Wi-Fi extender only partially papers over.

The install itself is straightforward when planned early — cable routed through loft space, wall cavities, or underfloor voids, terminated at both ends, and tested for performance before we hand it over. Planned alongside a rewire or renovation, it adds very little extra disruption; retrofitted into a finished space, it takes more care but is still very achievable in most properties.

concerns.q: Will cabling be visible once it's finished?
concerns.a: No — cable is routed through voids and terminated at a flush-mounted faceplate, the same as a standard socket.

concerns.q: Can you set up a small business network from scratch?
concerns.a: Yes, including planning point positions, running cabling, and terminating a patch panel if your setup needs one.

name: Extractor Fan Installation
shortDesc: Bathroom, kitchen, and utility room extractor fans fitted to Building Regulations Part F.
intro: Bathrooms and kitchens without proper extraction lead to damp, mould, and peeling paint faster than most people expect. We install extractor fans correctly wired and ducted to meet Building Regulations, not just screwed to a ceiling and left.
highlights: Bathroom, kitchen, and utility room extractor fans
Correctly ducted to the outside, not just vented into a loft space
Humidity-sensing and timer-controlled options
Wired to the correct switching, including light-linked fans
whyUs: Fans ducted properly to the outside, not left venting into a loft
Humidity sensor and timer options set up correctly, not left on default
Experience with bathroom zoning and safe isolation around wet areas
Straightforward advice on which fan actually suits the room
signs: You've got condensation, damp patches, or mould developing in a bathroom
Your kitchen retains cooking smells and steam long after cooking
There's no fan at all in a windowless bathroom or utility room
Your current fan is noisy, weak, or you're not sure it's ducted outside
You're renovating a bathroom or kitchen and want extraction planned in properly

faqs.q: Is an extractor fan a legal requirement in bathrooms?
faqs.a: Building Regulations Part F requires adequate ventilation in bathrooms and kitchens, particularly where there's no openable window — a correctly specified extractor fan is the standard way to meet this.

faqs.q: Where should extractor fan ducting actually go?
faqs.a: Out to the external air, ideally by the shortest practical route — venting into a loft space instead is a common shortcut that just moves the damp problem rather than solving it.

faqs.q: What's the difference between timer and humidity-sensing fans?
faqs.a: A timer runs for a set period after the light's switched on; a humidity sensor detects moisture in the air and runs automatically regardless of the light switch — useful for baths or showers left running without the light on.

faqs.q: Can a fan be wired to run with the light?
faqs.a: Yes, light-linked switching is a common and straightforward setup, alongside a timer overrun if you want the fan to keep running briefly after the light's off.

faqs.q: How noisy should a new fan be?
faqs.a: Modern fans are considerably quieter than older units — if your fan's noticeably loud, it may be undersized, poorly mounted, or simply due for replacement.

deepDive.heading: Why Ducting Route Matters More Than the Fan Itself
paragraphs: The fan unit gets most of the attention, but the ducting route is what actually determines whether extraction works. A fan venting into a loft space rather than outside just relocates the moisture problem, which is exactly what we find on a lot of older installations we're called out to fix.

Zoning matters just as much in a bathroom — fans and their switching need to be positioned and rated correctly for the wet zones they're near. We plan this properly as standard, along with humidity sensing or timer overrun depending on how the room's actually used, rather than fitting a generic fan and switch combination.

concerns.q: Will installing ducting mean going through an external wall or roof?
concerns.a: Usually yes, for a proper external vent — we'll explain the route and any making-good involved before starting.

concerns.q: Can you fix a fan that's already installed but not working properly?
concerns.a: Yes, we regularly diagnose and correct poorly ducted or wired existing fans, not just fit new ones.

name: Emergency Electrical Callouts
shortDesc: Same-day emergency electrician callouts for total power loss, sparking, and urgent faults.
intro: A total loss of power, a burning smell, or sparking from a socket isn't something to sit with until next week. We offer same-day emergency callouts across Glasgow for genuinely urgent electrical faults, with a fixed call-out charge agreed upfront.
highlights: Same-day response for genuine electrical emergencies
Total power loss, sparking, and burning smell callouts
Fixed call-out charge, agreed before we arrive
Same electrician handles diagnosis and repair on the visit
whyUs: We treat genuinely urgent faults as urgent, not next-week bookings
One fixed call-out charge, no surprise add-ons
Fully equipped to diagnose and fix most faults on the first visit
Available across Glasgow and the surrounding areas
signs: You've lost power to the whole property with no obvious cause
You can smell burning or see sparks from a socket, switch, or the consumer unit
A circuit has tripped and won't reset no matter what you try
You've got exposed or damaged wiring following an accident or storm damage
A commercial premises has lost power during trading hours

faqs.q: What counts as an electrical emergency?
faqs.a: Total loss of power with no clear cause, any burning smell or visible sparking, exposed live wiring, or a circuit that won't reset after multiple attempts — if in doubt, call us and describe what's happening.

faqs.q: What's your call-out charge?
faqs.a: It's a fixed charge agreed with you before we head out, so there's no surprise on arrival — any further work beyond diagnosis is quoted separately.

faqs.q: How fast can you actually get here?
faqs.a: We aim for same-day response on genuine emergencies across Glasgow and the surrounding areas — call rather than email for anything urgent.

faqs.q: Should I turn my main power off before you arrive?
faqs.a: Only if it's safe to access the consumer unit and you know how — if in doubt, leave it and we'll assess it safely on arrival.

faqs.q: Do you handle emergencies for businesses as well as homes?
faqs.a: Yes, including commercial premises losing power during trading hours, where getting back up and running quickly matters.

benefit: Same-Day Response When It Actually Can't Wait

deepDive.heading: What Happens When You Call an Electrical Emergency In
paragraphs: The first thing we do on the phone is work out whether it's genuinely urgent or can safely wait for a scheduled visit — total power loss, burning smells, and sparking get prioritised for same-day response, while a single dead socket with no other symptoms usually doesn't need an emergency rate.

On arrival, diagnosis comes first, using the same systematic approach as any fault-finding job, just faster. Most emergency callouts are resolved on the same visit; where a fault turns out to need parts or a bigger repair, we'll make the property safe first and explain clearly what happens next.

concerns.q: Is the call-out charge on top of the repair cost?
concerns.a: The call-out charge covers the visit and diagnosis; any repair work beyond that is quoted separately and agreed with you before we proceed.

concerns.q: What if it turns out not to be an emergency after all?
concerns.a: That's fine — we'd rather you call and it be minor than leave a genuine risk unchecked. We'll always tell you honestly what we find.
